newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline falls as U.K., German demand dries up.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline falls as U.K., German demand dries up.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices fell sharply on Monday as U.K. and German demand appeared to dry up and crude fell after Iraq said it agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up the oil-for-food deal, traders said.
"There is no demand," said one broker.
Eurograde barges fell about $7.50 to last trade at $208 fob ARA, after earlier deals at $210 fob Amsterdam-Rotterdam and prices heard as high as $215/217.
Regular unleaded traded at $202 fob ARA and ended the day at $200/$202, down $3 from Friday.

Barges moved lower with crude but activity was very quiet with traders waiting for Tuesday's U.K. budget and OPEC's meeting on Wednesday in Vienna where it is expected to roll over its ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.

The U.K. budget is expected to result in a tax on gasoline of 3.0-3.2 pence per litre. Traders disagreed as to whether prices would fall after the budget when inventories and refinery output flows out of the U.K.
Eurograde barges are already trading close to the Dec swaps, a barometer traders have used for prices next month.
Premium unleaded cargoes fell $4 to $224/$226 cif, $214/$216 fob, and regular unleaded to $213/$215 cif, $205/$207 fob.
